description: The screen half of Stage 1: a real player screen rather than a game drawn behind a debug overlay, the per-frame input push that makes FEAT-001's controls actually reach the core, a back control that stops the session properly, and the diagnostics kept whole. Touches native/ios/PlayerScreen.swift (new), native/ios/MetalCanvas.swift (one addition), native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift and native/ios/project.yml.
steps: Add the system dimension to CoreCatalog without creating a second routing table. Replace the literal `routes` dictionary with ONE table of route records carrying both the core id and the GameSystem, and DERIVE `routes` from it with mapValues so the two provably cannot drift. Everything that already reads `routes`, `core(forExtension:)` and `routeLabel(forExtension:)` keeps working unchanged, and the launchableExtensions = importableExtensions minus bin derivation is untouched.
Add `system(forExtension:)` so the player screen can ask what kind of pad to draw from the launched entry's extension, which is the same key the core was routed on.

Add the player session state to EngineHost: `activeEntry: LibraryEntry?` set at the end of a successful launch and cleared on stop, `paused`, and `showDiagnostics`. activeEntry is what switches the root view, and keying it off the entry rather than a bool means the player screen knows the filename, the extension and therefore the system without a second lookup.

Set activeEntry in launch(entry:) on the success path ONLY, beside the existing `running = true`, and clear it in stopSession(). Do not otherwise touch launch: the ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING comment, the stop-before-ensureCoreLoaded sequence, the breadcrumb strings and the single engine.launch call site all stay exactly as they are.

Add `leavePlayer()` on EngineHost: it calls the existing stopSession(), which is what releases the core under the Drop retention policy, then writes a distinct status line naming the game that was stopped, then clears paused so a later launch does not inherit a stale pause. It must not call ensureCoreLoaded, and it must not pre-empt the next launch's own stop.

Add pause and resume actions that call engine.pause() and engine.resume(nowMillis:) with CACurrentMediaTime() * 1000.0, the same clock MetalCanvas already uses for didBecomeActive, and keep `paused` in step with them so the control can show which state it is in.

Add a save-state action that calls the already-exposed engine.saveState(), writes the bytes next to the game in Documents as <name>.state, and reports the byte count or the specific error. Every branch writes its own line: no core loaded, the engine refused, the write failed, and success with a size.

Add ONE property to MetalCanvas: `var gamepadSource: (() -> PadFrame)?`, read inside the existing display-link tick immediately BEFORE engine.tick and pushed with engine.applyGamepad(port: 0, buttons:axes:). This is the whole reason held buttons work: apply_standard_gamepad replaces the gamepad source layer wholesale on every call, so pushing only on touch-down would have the next frame clear the press. The tick already runs on the main thread (CADisplayLink added to .main) and already calls a closure that writes to EngineHost's published properties, so this introduces no new isolation boundary. Nothing else in MetalCanvas changes: not configureLayer, not syncDrawableSize, not attachEngine, not adoptEngineMetalObjects, not one lifecycle method.

Keep exactly ONE MetalCanvasView mounted for the app's lifetime, at the bottom of the root ZStack, and switch what covers it. Unmounting it to push a player screen would tear down the CAMetalLayer that the engine attached to and force a second attachMetal against a new layer, which is the one part of this app that cannot be tested here; the invariant says do not touch the graphics attach path beyond what a player screen genuinely needs, and it does not need that.

Split the root view: when host.activeEntry is nil, an opaque library screen covers the canvas; when it is set, the player chrome and the touch controls sit over it. The picture is already aspect-correct on black without any view resizing, because gfx/renderer.rs defaults to ScaleMode::AspectFit (renderer.rs:304) and letterboxes inside the surface itself.

Build the player chrome in a new file native/ios/PlayerScreen.swift: a back chevron top-left that calls leavePlayer(), the game name, and a thin telemetry strip of fps, frames, dropped, audio latency in ms and the core id.

Derive audio latency honestly: queued frames over 48000, times 1000. That is a fact rather than a guess, because output_sample_rate defaults to 48000 (bridge.rs:143) and set_output_sample_rate is NOT exposed through UniFFI, so nothing on iOS can change it. Say so in a comment naming the line, so the day audio output is wired the number is corrected rather than quietly wrong.

Put the session controls (pause, reset, save state, diagnostics toggle) in the TOP bar, NOT in the thumb band. This is the deliberate fix for the bug docs/mobile-player.png captures: that layout put pause, volume, Save state and four selectors in the same band as the D-pad and the face buttons, and they collided. Separating session controls from gameplay controls by region means the two can never fight, in either orientation.

Keep every diagnostic. A thin always-visible status line shows host.status at the bottom of the chrome, and the full block (the phase banner, status, cores, bios, gpu and the frame counters) is behind the diagnostics toggle, on BOTH the library screen and the player screen. No string is deleted and every existing message is still displayable, because on a sideloaded build with no debugger the HUD is the only debugger there is.
Release the touch state when the player screen goes away or the app leaves the foreground, so a finger down at that moment cannot leave a direction held.

Add both new Swift files to native/ios/project.yml under targets.Continuum.sources. The list is explicit; a file missing from it compiles nowhere and the feature simply does not exist on device, with no error to read.
acceptance_criteria: Tapping a game opens a dedicated player screen; the library is not visible behind it and the debug HUD is not drawn over the picture by default.
The back control calls the existing stopSession(), so the core is released under the Drop retention policy, and returns to the library with a distinct status line naming the game that stopped.
The emulated picture is aspect-correct on black, achieved by the renderer's existing AspectFit rather than by resizing the Metal view.
A thin telemetry strip shows fps, frames, dropped, audio latency in ms and the running core id.
The pad state is pushed every frame from the display-link tick, immediately before engine.tick, so a held button stays held across frames.
applyGamepad is called with port 0, 16 booleans and 4 floats.
The touch controls match the launched game's system, resolved through the same single routing table the core was resolved on.
Session controls live in the top bar and gameplay controls in the bottom band, so no control overlaps another or the picture in either orientation.
Pause, reset and save state work through the already-exposed engine calls, and each failure path writes its own distinct status string.
Every diagnostic string that existed before is still reachable: the thin status line is always visible and the full block is one toggle away on both screens.
CoreCatalog still has exactly ONE extension routing table, with `routes` derived from it rather than restated, and launchableExtensions is still importableExtensions minus bin.
Exactly one engine.launch call site, one MetalCanvasView mounted for the app's lifetime, one MTLDevice still created by Rust and read back by Swift.
The picker machinery, ensureCoreLoaded, refreshLibrary, importFiles, deleteEntries and LibraryEntry are unchanged.
Both new files are listed in project.yml sources and the YAML still parses.
No em dashes anywhere in the changed files.
verification: swiftc -frontend -parse on all four files under native/ios/ -> exit 0 each. SPELL-CHECK ONLY, so the items below are by eye.
By eye: the applyGamepad call passes port: 0 and arrays of 16 and 4, and sits BEFORE engine.tick in the same tick.
By eye: MetalCanvas's diff is the one new property and the two lines that use it, nothing else.
By eye: launch(entry:) still stops before ensureCoreLoaded, still carries the ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING comment, and still has the single engine.launch call.
By eye: everything that reads EngineHost is inside a SwiftUI view body or an @MainActor method, and the only closure the display link calls into is the same shape as the existing onTelemetry.
By eye: every status string that existed on master still exists, and both the thin line and the full block are reachable from both screens.
python3 -c yaml.safe_load on native/ios/project.yml -> valid, and both new files appear under targets.Continuum.sources.
cargo test -> 74 passing, proving no Rust changed.
git diff --name-only -> only native/ios/** plus the task directory.
grep for em dashes across the changed files -> no match.
The .ipa build, the on-screen result and every gesture are verified ONLY by the orchestrator's CI run and device test.
findings: CoreCatalog gained the system dimension WITHOUT a second routing table: `routeTable` is now the one literal, holding core id plus GameSystem per extension, and `routes` is derived from it with mapValues, so the old key set and every existing reader are unchanged and the two cannot drift. EngineHost gained activeEntry, paused and showDiagnostics; activeEntry is set only on launch's success path beside the existing running = true and cleared in stopSession, which means the load-bearing order (stopSession, THEN ensureCoreLoaded) and the single engine.launch call site are untouched. leavePlayer() delegates to the existing stopSession() rather than calling engine.stop() itself, so there is still exactly one place that stops a session. MetalCanvas's entire diff is one property, `gamepadSource`, plus the two lines in tick that read it and call applyGamepad BEFORE engine.tick. That ordering is the feature: apply_standard_gamepad replaces the gamepad layer wholesale, so a push per frame is what holds a button down and a push per touch-down would be cleared by the next frame. The display link is already added to .main and the tick already calls a closure that writes EngineHost's published properties, so no new isolation boundary appears and the graphics attach path is untouched. ONE MetalCanvasView stays mounted for the app's lifetime at the bottom of the root ZStack and the screens cover it, because unmounting it would tear down the attached CAMetalLayer and force a second attachMetal that nothing here can test. The picture needed no resizing to be aspect-correct: gfx/renderer.rs defaults to ScaleMode::AspectFit (renderer.rs:304) and letterboxes inside the surface. Audio latency is queued frames over 48000 times 1000, which is a derivation and not a guess, because output_sample_rate defaults to 48000 at bridge.rs:143 and set_output_sample_rate is not exposed through UniFFI, so nothing on iOS can change it; the comment names the line so the number gets corrected when audio output lands. TWO THINGS THE REFERENCE SCREENSHOT ASKS FOR THAT CANNOT BE BUILT WITHOUT TOUCHING RUST, and are therefore deferred to FEAT-006 rather than faked: the aspect, filter, speed and scale selectors need set_scale_mode, set_filter and the pacer's speed multiplier exported through UniFFI, and volume needs the mute or gain control exported; none of the five is in uniffi_api.rs, whose input surface ends at connected_pads. The 'MB core' figure has no engine API at all. The session controls were moved into the top bar deliberately: docs/mobile-player.png is itself a capture of the overlap bug, caused by putting pause, volume, Save state and four selectors in the same band as the D-pad and face buttons, so separating session controls from gameplay controls by region is what stops it recurring.
